title: Small-sphere models of G2874 give larger dust radii and unbound graphite
abstract: We test the use of a 230 K blackbody radius to assign at least 13 orbits to the 19-year faint state of G2874. We combine published optical-slope and infrared-colour summaries with Mie heating and radiation forces for single-size silicate and graphite spheres. At an assumed luminosity of 0.8 solar and mass of 0.95 solar, spheres with optical slopes of 2.5-2.8 lie at 2.99-4.08 au for silicate and 11.47-11.91 au for graphite. Silicate circular dust periods are 5.96-14.66 years. The graphite force is 3.05-3.46 times gravity, so its 40-year gravity-only period is not an orbit. This force stays above 1.51 across nine tested stellar mass and luminosity pairs. A broad-band stress test retains the distinction. The blackbody orbit count is therefore not a lower bound. The result does not identify the dust: the input epochs differ, the optical selection uses only a slope, and we do not fit a size distribution or the full SED. Code, model grids, checks and external input hashes are included. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-c1a937f5b486; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.
